key_insight: The paper argues that genuine recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires AI systems to not only improve their outputs, but also to autonomously improve how they learn, adapt, and optimize future improvement cycles.
engineering_relevance: For computational science and engineering, RSI points toward AI agents that can continuously upgrade scientific workflows, software development, and embodied control with increasing autonomy.
method: Uses the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose limitations in current LLMs.
Defines a staged RSI roadmap: execution autonomy, strategy autonomy, experience acquisition autonomy, environment adaptation autonomy, and recursive meta-improvement.
Compares RSI requirements across scientific discovery, embodied intelligence, and software engineering scenarios.
evidence_signal: The abstract cites preliminary empirical evidence and industry practices, but does not report detailed quantitative benchmarks or a specific evaluation dataset.
watch_item: A major challenge is ensuring that recursive improvement remains safe, measurable, and robust rather than amplifying errors or drifting from intended goals.
paper_title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
